questions.question: Which of the following is a component of the SHG-bank linkage program in India?
questions.option_1: Microfinance institutions providing loans directly to SHGs
questions.option_2: Banks providing loans to individual members of SHGs
questions.option_3: Non-governmental organisations providing capacity building training to SHGs
questions.option_4: State government providing subsidies to SHGs for credit
questions.solution: The SHG-Bank Linkage Model, launched by NABARD in 1992-93, involves banks directly lending to SHGs. The SHGs then manage the distribution and guarantee of loans for their individual members.

questions.question: If assets of a bank are greater than liabilities, it will be recorded as:
questions.solution:
Net worth (or equity) is calculated using the formula:
Assets - Liabilities = Net Worth.
It represents the actual ownership value of the business once all debts (liabilities) are covered by the assets.

questions.question: Which of the following is Fisher's equation of exchange?
questions.solution:
The Fisher Equation is MV = PT, where:
  • M = Money Supply
  • V = Velocity of circulation
  • P = Price Level
  • T = Volume of transactions

questions.question: The Working Group under the chairmanship of _______ in the year _______ proposed a new intermediate monetary aggregate to be referred to as NM2.
questions.solution: In 1998, a working group led by Dr. Y.V. Reddy proposed new monetary aggregates, including NM2 (Narrow Money 2), to help the RBI better monitor liquidity and control inflation.

questions.question: The term ‘Microfinancing’ was first used in the 1970s during the development of Grameen Bank of Bangladesh, which was founded by _____.
questions.solution: Muhammad Yunus is known as the founder of modern microfinance. He established the Grameen Bank in Bangladesh and was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006 for his work in microcredit.

questions.question: Which of the following is issued by commercial banks at a discount on face value?
questions.solution: Certificates of Deposits (CDs) are short-term, negotiable instruments issued by commercial banks at a discount on their face value. Note that Treasury Bills are issued by the government, not commercial banks.

questions.question: What is the primary aim of Regional Rural Banks in India?
questions.solution: Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were established in 1975 to develop the rural economy by providing credit and banking facilities to small farmers, agricultural laborers, and rural artisans.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Reserve Bank of India’s Central Office was initially established in Kolkata.
Reason (R): Kolkata was the capital of India in 1935.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_3: A is true but R is false.
questions.option_4: A is false but R is true.
questions.solution: Assertion A is true: the RBI was established in 1935 with its office in Kolkata. However, Reason R is false: the capital of India had already been shifted from Kolkata to Delhi in 1911.

questions.question: In 2000-01, NABARD instituted Micro Finance Development Fund with a corpus of ________.
questions.solution: NABARD set up the Micro Finance Development Fund with an initial corpus of ₹100 crores to promote and support Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and microfinance institutions in India.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Open Market Operations (OMO):
1. OMOs are conducted by the Ministry of Finance.
2. OMOs are used to control money supply and liquidity.
3. RBI sells government securities to absorb liquidity.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. OMOs are conducted by the RBI (not the Ministry of Finance). To reduce liquidity, the RBI sells securities; to increase it, the RBI buys them.

questions.question: Rotating Savings and Credit Association (ROSCA) was introduced by Shirley Ardener in the year ________.
questions.solution: ROSCA was introduced by Shirley Ardener in 1964. It serves as an informal financial system where a group of individuals act as a financial institution by rotating savings.

questions.question: Which of the following banks is in charge of India’s banking and monetary system?
questions.solution: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank of India. It regulates the monetary policy, currency circulation, and the overall banking system.

questions.question: Selling of bonds by the RBI will cause money supply to __________.
questions.option_2: No relationship exists between selling bonds and money supply
questions.solution: When the RBI sells bonds/securities, it takes money out of the banking system (sucking liquidity), which leads to a decrease in the money supply.

questions.question: If the value / percentage of the cash reserve ratio falls, then the value of money multiplier ________.
questions.solution: The money multiplier is inversely related to the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR). If CRR falls, banks have more money to lend, which increases (rises) the money multiplier.

questions.question: Who issued guidelines for the microfinance institutions in India?
questions.solution: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the regulator for microfinance in India. It defines microloans and sets interest rate and repayment guidelines for MFIs.

questions.question: When RBI decides to decrease the repo rate, money supply will _________.
questions.option_4: initially stay constant and then decrease
questions.solution: A decrease in the repo rate makes borrowing cheaper for commercial banks. This encourages them to lend more to the public, thereby increasing the money supply.

questions.question: For providing a non-microfinance loan to a low-income household, there is a limit of ____ on monthly loan repayment obligations of a household as a percentage of monthly household income.
questions.solution: The RBI has set a limit of 50% on monthly loan repayments relative to household income to prevent low-income families from falling into excessive debt.

questions.question: What distinguishes a bank from other financial institutions?
questions.solution: While many institutions lend money, the acceptance of demand deposits from the general public is the unique primary function that defines a bank.

questions.question: ________ is an instrument under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) at which RBI lends to commercial banks.
questions.solution: The Repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks against securities under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF).

questions.question: The maximum limit on microfinance loans for NBFCs other than NBFC-MFIs is _________.
questions.solution: The RBI increased the limit for microfinance loans by non-MFI NBFCs to 25% of their total assets (up from 10%). Simultaneously, the requirement for NBFC-MFIs was reduced to 75% of total loan assets.

questions.question: In the concept of money supply, M4 refers to ________.
questions.option_4: M1+ time deposits of the public with banks
questions.solution:
In RBI's money supply metrics:
  • M1: Narrow Money
  • M3: Broad Money
  • M4: M3 + Total Post Office Deposits (excluding NSC).

questions.question:
Identify the correct statement in the context of money supply:
i) Money supply refers to the total volume of money held by public at a particular point of time
ii) Money supply is a flow concept
iii) M1 is the most liquid measure of money supply
questions.solution: Statement (i) is correct as money supply is a stock concept (measured at a point in time), not a flow concept. Statement (iii) is also correct because M1 is the most liquid measure.

questions.question: Which of the following is a function performed by commercial banks in India?
questions.solution: Credit creation is a primary function of commercial banks. Functions like issuing currency and credit control are handled by the Central Bank (RBI).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a Micro Finance Institution (MFI)?
questions.option_1: A financial institution lending only to corporates
questions.option_2: A non-banking institution lending to poor and low-income households without collateral
questions.option_4: A cooperative society registered with SEBI
questions.solution: An MFI provides small loans and financial services to low-income individuals or underserved populations, usually without requiring collateral.

questions.question: Which of the following microfinance institutions was established in India at the time of independence?
questions.solution: Rural Cooperatives have been a part of India's landscape since before and around the time of independence. Other models like SHGs and Grameen-style banking emerged much later (1970s-1990s).
